summary: SIEM ingest watermark drift causing duplicate events; request for retention & signed evidence bundle
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (MonetaBank) reports repeated duplicate audit events in their SIEM ingestion (Splunk) for a subset of webhook-delivered activity ledgers over a 48h window. The customer requires a signed evidence bundle enumerating delivered batches, per-batch checksums, resume tokens, and retention metadata to support a regulatory case and reconcile their retention policy enforcement.

Impact:
- Duplicate events seen in Splunk causing false positives in SOC alerts and inflated storage costs.
- Customer's compliance team has raised an escalation with legal; they require cryptographically verifiable delivery records for a specific 36-hour window (2026-03-09 16:00 UTC to 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC).
- P1 due to enterprise SLA and potential regulatory audit.

Timeline & Observed Behavior:
1) 2026-03-09 16:10 UTC - MonetaBank support reports an increase in duplicate event counts for tenant moneta-prod-1 (reported via #support-moneta slack).
2) Customer provided Splunk ingest statistics showing repeated event_id hashes and a rising dedup metric at index time.
3) On our side, webhooks to their HEC endpoint show successful 200 responses from the customer gateway with occasional 5xx responses upstream during the window.
4) Resumption tokens for some batches are identical across two deliveries and batch manifests show overlapping sequence ranges.

Steps to reproduce (support-side):
1) Retrieve delivery logs for tenant moneta-prod-1 for 2026-03-09 15:50 - 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC.
2) Filter audit-export events by delivery_id and sequence_range; identify any overlapping ranges or duplicate resume_token values.
3) Correlate our delivery manifest with the customer's HEC ack timestamps.

Attachments customer provided:
- Splunk index count CSV (split by hour)
- Sample of duplicated events (3 examples)
- HEC ingest timestamps and indexer GUIDs

Expected behavior:
- Each audit batch delivered once; resume tokens unique per batch; manifests contain non-overlapping sequence ranges.

Customer asks:
- Signed evidence bundle (per-batch manifest, sha256 checksums, resume tokens, RFC3161 timestamps) for the window specified.
- Short-term mitigation suggestion to prevent further duplicates (ingest-side dedupe guidance + temporary backoff settings).
comments: 2026-03-12 09:34 - Maya Patel (Support): Customer opened via support portal and attached Splunk counts and three example events. Escalated to SRE due to batch/resume token concerns.

2026-03-12 11:07 - Noah Thompson (SRE): Initial triage - observed a small cluster of delivery retries from the scheduling service between 2026-03-09T16:02Z and 2026-03-09T16:45Z correlated with elevated response latencies to the customer's HEC gateway. Collecting delivery manifests and routing traces now.

2026-03-12 13:22 - Elena Ruiz (Customer Success, on-call): Reiterated customer's compliance deadline: legal would like the evidence bundle by 2026-03-14 EOD. Asked for ETA and temporary dedupe options at ingestion side.

2026-03-12 16:05 - Noah Thompson (SRE): Posted candidate hypothesis: scheduler re-queued batches when webhook latencies exceeded 30s threshold; requeue path didn't always mark the original manifest as superseded leading to two valid manifests with overlapping ranges and identical resume_token in rare race. Logging patch and additional tracing added to the scheduler today.

2026-03-13 08:10 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer confirmed they are seeing fewer duplicates after we suggested enabling Splunk dedup at index_time as a temporary measure. They still need the signed bundle for the window.

2026-03-14 10:41 - Noah Thompson (SRE): Uploaded signed evidence bundle to secure S3 presigned URL and notified customer via secure channel. Bundle contains per-batch manifests, sha256 checksums, RFC3161 timestamps, and delivery trace logs. Also included a short remediation runbook.
investigation_notes: Collected delivery manifests for moneta-prod-1 for the full window; found 7 batches where sequence ranges overlapped by one or two messages.

Scheduler logs show two code paths that can trigger a retry: 'latency_requeue' and 'delivery_error_retry'. In 5 of 7 overlapping batches the requeue was triggered by 'latency_requeue' and the in-memory marker that prevents duplicate activation was not persisted due to a transient memcache timeout.

Resume_token generation uses (tenant,shard,epoch,seq_range)-based hashing. In the race we observed, the second delivery reused the same derived resume_token because seq_range calculation used end-exclusive semantics; off-by-one in the rounding produced identical tokens for the overlapping runs.

Customer HEC acks were 200 for both deliveries in 4 cases; in 3 cases the customer's gateway returned 502 for the first attempt and 200 for the retry, which explains why customer index shows duplicates when both deliveries were ultimately accepted by their downstream indexer.
No evidence of malicious replays or third-party resend. All deliveries originated from our scheduler with identical client_cert subjects (pinned).
resolution_notes: Immediate workaround provided: advise customer to enable index-time deduplication in Splunk for event_id and to apply a 5-minute sliding window dedupe to suppress transient duplicate spikes.

Short-term mitigation implemented by infra: patched scheduler to persist 'delivery-activation' markers to redis before enqueuing a retry; deployed 2026-03-13 02:18 UTC (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2147). This prevents the race that created overlapping active manifests.

Long-term fix: updated resume_token derivation to include monotonic delivery UUID and made seq_range semantics end-inclusive consistently. Rollout plan: canary in us-east for 48h then global. Related PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2150.

Evidence bundle contents delivered to customer: per-batch manifest (JSON), sha256 checksums, RFC3161-signed timestamp bundle (via HSM), delivery traces (truncated), and a signed manifest index. Uploaded to secure S3 presigned URL: https://s3.redwood-internal/moneta/evidence/SUP-583214-bundle-20260314.tar.gz (link delivered via customer-only channel).
Follow-ups: create a support runbook for 'watermark-drift' incidents, add synthetic test to verify resume_token uniqueness under retry, and schedule postmortem with SRE/CS/Customer on 2026-03-18.
Status: evidence delivered and customer acknowledged receipt. Work items remain open for the long-term rollout and runbook (tracked in INT-4421 and INT-4488).
